correctness.rationale: A long palindromic prefix induces a global reflection. Composing reflections fixes the unique center congruence for all long palindrome factors. Lengthening a factor by p yields PL(n+p)<=PL(n); in a factorization of length >p^2 one factor can be shortened by p, proving the reverse. Published translation lemma supplies L(j+p)>=L(j) globally, needed for M to appear in the stabilized window. The single large palindromic-prefix residue contributes P(N)=N/p+O(1), while exactly t of p stable residues maximize L. Direct independent dynamic programming tested 190 primitive binary palindrome-rich periods up to seven, including threshold, maximum, and t range; finite tests are not the proof. Caveat: the cited published translation lemma was not independently checked in its original full text.

final_claim: For every nonconstant purely periodic right-infinite word with minimal period p>=2 and infinitely many palindromic prefixes, PL(prefix_n)<=p and PL(prefix_{n+p})=PL(prefix_n) for n>=p(p-1)+1. The ratio |T_w(N)|/P_w(N) tends to an integer t between 1 and p-1, computable from the stable window; two-run words attain t=p-1.
